answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by making each identity earn its throughput through bonded, attested work. A newcomer must forge a record one verified job at a time: counterparties sign each completed task, and the agent posts a small refundable bond per job, so a single inlet of trust opens only after real work is delivered. Influence and payment limits grow with that history toward a wider horizon. An attacker spinning up thousands of fake agents must fund a bond and complete genuine work for each one, so a Sybil crowd costs real money and time for almost no extra influence.
